q: After a work has been awarded to a joint venture of firms, a change in the composition or shareholding of the joint venture:

options.A: Can be made freely by the members among themselves at any time
options.B: Can be made by the lead member alone by expelling a defaulting member at his discretion
options.C: Cannot be made without the prior approval of the Railways, the award having been made on the pooled credentials of the members as constituted
options.D: Takes place automatically if any one member of the venture becomes insolvent

e: A change in the composition or shareholding of a joint venture after award cannot be made without prior approval of the Railways, because the award was made on the pooled credentials of the members as constituted at award.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. A Micro or Small Enterprise which produces proof of its registration with the prescribed registering authority is exempted from furnishing the Earnest Money Deposit for participating in a tender.
2. An enterprise so exempted from Earnest Money Deposit is, on being awarded the work, also exempted from furnishing the Performance Guarantee or Security Deposit for the work.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Statement 1 is correct: a Micro or Small Enterprise producing proof of registration with the prescribed authority is exempted from Earnest Money Deposit. Statement 2 is wrong because that exemption does not extend to Performance Guarantee or Security Deposit on award.

q: Payment for work executed on a 'day work' basis under a contract is made on the basis of:

options.A: A lump sum fixed in advance for the whole of such work
options.B: The measurements of the finished work recorded in the Measurement Book at the end of the contract
options.C: The rates quoted by the contractor for similar items in his tender, without any daily record
options.D: The labour, materials and plant actually employed, recorded day to day in day-work sheets signed by the representative of the Engineer and the contractor

e: Day work is paid on the labour, materials and plant actually employed, recorded day to day in day-work sheets signed by the representative of the Engineer and the contractor, under the GCC day work provisions.

q: On the expiry or termination of a services contract, the outgoing contractor is required to:

options.A: Retain the records and Railway materials in his custody until his claims under the next contract are settled
options.B: Hand over the premises, the records and any Railway materials in his custody and withdraw his staff in an orderly manner, so that the service continues without disruption under the successor arrangement
options.C: Hand over his staff to the Railways, who must engage them directly thereafter
options.D: Continue the service indefinitely on his own without any sanction, until a successor is appointed

e: On expiry or termination of a services contract, the outgoing contractor must hand over the premises, records and Railway materials in his custody and withdraw his staff in an orderly manner so the service continues without disruption.

q: Under an Annual Maintenance Contract for equipment, the contracting agency is required to:

options.A: Attend only to breakdown repairs, periodical preventive maintenance not forming part of such a contract
options.B: Carry out the preventive maintenance of the equipment departmentally through the Railway's own staff
options.C: Carry out scheduled preventive maintenance visits at the prescribed periodicity, in addition to attending to breakdown calls as and when they arise
options.D: Attend the equipment only when it has failed completely and stopped working

e: Under an Annual Maintenance Contract the agency must carry out scheduled preventive maintenance visits at the prescribed periodicity in addition to attending breakdown calls as they arise.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. A licence of railway land is personal to the licensee, who cannot transfer, assign or sublet the licensed land to another person without the permission of the Railways.
2. A licence of railway land does not pass to any other person as a matter of right; continued occupation of the land by another person requires a fresh permission or licence from the Railways.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Both are correct: a licence of railway land is personal to the licensee, who cannot transfer, assign or sublet it without Railway permission, and it does not pass to another person as of right; fresh permission is needed for another occupant.

q: Where a licensee of railway land persistently defaults in the payment of the licence fee and other charges payable by him:

options.A: The licence can never be terminated on the ground of non-payment of the charges
options.B: The licence can be terminated by the Railways in accordance with its conditions and the land resumed, after following the prescribed procedure
options.C: The arrears are automatically converted into a lease of the land in favour of the licensee
options.D: The Railways must renew the licence and bear the loss of the unpaid charges

e: On persistent default in payment of licence fee and charges, the licence can be terminated in accordance with its conditions and the land resumed after following the prescribed procedure.

q: A loss of public money or of railway property comes to the notice of the executive, whether due to fraud, negligence or accident. The action required in the first instance is that:

options.A: The loss is reported only at the end of the year along with the completion reports of works
options.B: A loss of small amount need not be reported or enquired into at all
options.C: The loss is first written off from the books and an enquiry is held afterwards only if Audit insists on it
options.D: The loss is reported promptly to the higher authority and to Accounts and Audit, and an enquiry into it is ordered, without waiting for its write-off

e: A loss of public money or railway property, whether by fraud, negligence or accident, must be reported promptly to the higher authority and to Accounts and Audit and an enquiry ordered at once, without waiting for write-off, as per the GFR loss provisions.

q: The balances outstanding under Miscellaneous Works Advances and other works suspense heads are kept under control by:

options.A: Periodical, age-wise review of the outstanding balances by the executive and Accounts, with prompt action for the recovery or adjustment of the old items
options.B: A review carried out only when the contractor concerned claims a refund from the Railways
options.C: Automatic write-off of every balance which remains outstanding for more than one year
options.D: A review carried out by the contractor, who alone maintains the record of the balances

e: Balances under Miscellaneous Works Advances and works suspense heads are controlled by periodical age-wise review by the executive and Accounts, with prompt action for recovery or adjustment of old items.

q: A proposal for a work which is put up for the concurrence of Finance must, among other things, indicate:

options.A: The allocation, that is, the head of account to which the expenditure is chargeable, and the availability of funds or provision for it, so that concurrence is accorded with reference to the correct head and grant
options.B: Only the name of the contractor by whom the work is proposed to be executed
options.C: The rates at which the tender for the work will finally be accepted
options.D: The date on which the completion report of the work will be submitted

e: A proposal put up for Finance concurrence must indicate the allocation, that is the head of account chargeable, and availability of funds or provision for it, so concurrence is given with reference to the correct head and grant.

q: Under the price variation clause of a works contract, the adjustment for the material component of the work is computed with reference to:

options.A: The All India Consumer Price Index for Industrial Workers
options.B: The Wholesale Price Index numbers for the relevant materials, as specified in the contract
options.C: The actual purchase bills produced by the contractor in every case
options.D: The rates given in the Unified Standard Schedule of Rates for the current year

e: Under the price variation clause, adjustment for the material component is computed with reference to the Wholesale Price Index numbers for the relevant materials as specified in the contract.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. A works contractor is bound to comply, at his own cost, with all the statutory requirements applicable to the work and to the labour engaged by him, such as the labour, safety and tax laws, during the execution of the work.
2. Once a running bill of the contractor has been paid by the Railways, the contractor stands absolved of his statutory defaults in respect of the work covered by that bill.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Statement 1 is correct: the contractor must comply at his own cost with all statutory requirements for the work and labour. Statement 2 is wrong because payment of a running bill does not absolve him of statutory defaults for that work.

q: The mobilisation advance granted to a works contractor at the commencement of a work:

options.A: Is a general loan which the contractor may utilise on any work or purpose of his choice
options.B: Need not be accounted for by the contractor to the Railways in any manner
options.C: Is converted into an outright grant in favour of the contractor if the work is delayed
options.D: Is granted for mobilisation for that particular work and must be utilised for that work itself, its diversion to other works or purposes being a breach of the contract conditions

e: Mobilisation advance is granted for mobilisation for that particular work and must be utilised for that work itself; its diversion to other works or purposes is a breach of the contract conditions.

q: 'Taking over' of a completed work, as distinguished from the issue of its completion certificate, means that:

options.A: Both expressions mean the same thing and both are recorded by the contractor himself
options.B: The taking over of the work is recorded by the Accounts office before the completion certificate is issued in every case
options.C: The completion certificate records the Engineer's certification that the work has been completed in accordance with the contract, whereas taking over is the act by which the department which will use and maintain the asset accepts it from the executing agency for use
options.D: The completion certificate is issued by the department which will use the asset and the taking over is done by the Tender Committee

e: The completion certificate is the Engineer certification that the work is completed per the contract, whereas taking over is the act by which the department that will use and maintain the asset accepts it from the executing agency for use.

q: Where other contractors or departmental agencies are also working at the same site as a works contractor:

options.A: The contractor may deny them access to the site until his own work is fully completed
options.B: The contractor is required to afford them reasonable facilities and to co-ordinate his work with theirs, the Engineer deciding the sequence of operations where they interface with each other
options.C: Such other agencies can be allowed to work at the site only after the defect liability period of the contractor's work has expired
options.D: The co-ordination of the agencies at the site is the responsibility of the Tender Committee

e: A contractor must afford reasonable facilities to other contractors or departmental agencies working at the same site and co-ordinate with them, the Engineer deciding the sequence where their operations interface, under the GCC.

q: During the execution of a work, the contractor notices a discrepancy or an error in the drawings or specifications issued to him for the work. The correct course for him is to:

options.A: Follow whichever of the conflicting drawings he prefers and proceed with the work
options.B: Get the discrepancy resolved by the Tender Committee after the work is completed
options.C: Proceed with the work on his own interpretation and claim extra payment for it as a matter of right
options.D: Bring the discrepancy to the notice of the Engineer and obtain his instructions before proceeding with the affected work

e: On noticing a discrepancy or error in drawings or specifications, the contractor must bring it to the notice of the Engineer and obtain his instructions before proceeding with the affected work.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Development Fund of the Railways is used mainly for works of passenger amenities, staff welfare and unremunerative but necessary operating improvements.
2. The Capital Fund of the Railways is used for financing capital works chargeable to Capital when budgetary support under the Capital head is inadequate.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Both are correct: the Development Fund finances passenger amenities, staff welfare and unremunerative but necessary operating improvements, and the Capital Fund finances capital works chargeable to Capital when budgetary support under Capital is inadequate.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Railway Safety Fund is the fund created for the wholesale renewal and replacement of track, signalling and other safety assets all over the Railways.
2. The Railway Safety Fund is used mainly for works connected with safety at level crossings, such as the construction of road over-bridges and road under-bridges and other level-crossing safety works.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Statement 2 is correct: the Railway Safety Fund is used mainly for safety works at level crossings such as road over-bridges, road under-bridges and other level crossing safety works. Statement 1 wrongly describes wholesale asset renewal, which is charged to other funds.

q: In a public-private partnership concession, the revenues of the project are ordinarily dealt with through an escrow arrangement, under which:

options.A: The concessionaire may keep the project revenues in his own general account, free of the provisions of the concession agreement
options.B: The earnest money of the bidders for the concession is deposited and retained till the end of the concession period
options.C: The escrow account is maintained by the Tender Committee for meeting the departmental charges of the project
options.D: The revenues are deposited in the escrow account and are applied in the order of priority laid down in the concession and escrow agreements, so that the project obligations and the lenders' dues are protected

e: Under the escrow arrangement in a PPP concession, project revenues are deposited in the escrow account and applied in the order of priority in the concession and escrow agreements, protecting project obligations and lenders dues.

q: A consultant engaged for the design of a railway project is ordinarily required to maintain professional indemnity insurance so that:

options.A: The consultant bears no liability at all for any error or negligence in the design prepared by him
options.B: The works executed to his design are insured against all risks during their execution
options.C: Loss arising from negligence or error in his professional services, including the design, is covered by the insurance
options.D: The insurance is taken out and paid for by the Railways on behalf of every consultant as a matter of course

e: Professional indemnity insurance of a consultant covers loss arising from negligence or error in his professional services including design, so the financial consequence of such errors is insured.

q: The 'carpet area' of a building means:

options.A: The built-up covered area of the building measured at the floor level of any storey
options.B: The usable floor area of the rooms, excluding the area occupied by walls, passages, verandahs and staircases
options.C: The total area of the plot of land on which the building is constructed
options.D: The area of the roof of the building measured at its topmost level

e: Carpet area is the usable floor area of the rooms, excluding the area occupied by walls, passages, verandahs and staircases; the built-up covered area at floor level is plinth area.

q: A temporary advance given to an officer for a specific official purpose differs from an imprest in that the temporary advance:

options.A: Is a standing advance which is recouped periodically on the basis of paid vouchers
options.B: Requires no account to be rendered for the amount advanced
options.C: Is advanced for that specific purpose and is adjusted or recovered on the rendering of the account for that purpose, and is not maintained as a standing recouped advance
options.D: Can be used for meeting any petty expenditure of the office as it arises

e: A temporary advance is given for a specific purpose and is adjusted or recovered on rendering of account for that purpose; unlike an imprest it is not a standing advance recouped periodically on paid vouchers.

q: In a nominal mix concrete, as distinguished from a design mix:

options.A: The proportions of cement and aggregates are prescribed nominally for the grade, without the proportions being established through laboratory design trials
options.B: The proportions of the ingredients are established through laboratory trials so as to achieve the specified strength and workability
options.C: No proportion of cement to aggregates is fixed at all
options.D: The contractor is free to adopt any proportion of ingredients he chooses

e: In a nominal mix the proportions of cement and aggregates are prescribed nominally for the grade, without laboratory design trials; design mix proportions are established through such trials.

q: Under the General Conditions of Contract for Services, if a service contractor persistently fails to render the services to the standard required by the contract, the Railways may, after following the procedure provided in the contract:

options.A: Pay the contractor also for the services which were not rendered by him
options.B: Extend the currency of the contract automatically for a further term
options.C: Direct the Tender Committee to render the services departmentally
options.D: Get the balance services rendered through another agency independently, the Performance Guarantee being encashed/forfeited and the balance services being got done without risk and cost of the defaulting contractor, as provided in the contract

e: Under the GCC for Services, on persistent failure after the prescribed procedure the Railways may get the balance services rendered through another agency independently, with the Performance Guarantee encashed or forfeited and without risk and cost of the defaulting contractor, as provided in that GCC.

q: Under a works contract, as regards inspection of the work during its execution:

options.A: The Engineer may inspect the work only after it has been completed
options.B: The contractor may refuse access to the place where materials for the work are being prepared
options.C: Inspection of the work during execution is carried out only by the Accounts office
options.D: The Engineer and his representatives are to be afforded access to the work, and to the places where materials are being prepared, together with facilities for inspection and testing

e: During execution the Engineer and his representatives must be afforded access to the work and to places where materials are being prepared, with facilities for inspection and testing, under the GCC inspection provisions.

q: The earnest money received from tenderers for a work is, until it is refunded, adjusted or forfeited:

options.A: Held as a deposit liability of the Railways and not treated as earnings, the amount being credited to the revenues of the Railways only when it is forfeited
options.B: Credited to the earnings of the Railways immediately on its receipt
options.C: Credited to Capital of the Railways on the opening of the tenders
options.D: Treated as the security deposit of the successful tenderer in every case

e: Earnest money is held as a deposit liability of the Railways and is not earnings; it is credited to revenues only when it is forfeited, and is otherwise refunded or adjusted.

q: Works for residential quarters, though excepted from the normal test of financial remunerativeness applied to remunerative works, are expected to satisfy the condition that:

options.A: No rent is recovered from the staff allotted the quarters
options.B: They are financed only from the Capital Fund of the Railways
options.C: The assessed rent recoverable for the quarters yields the prescribed return on the capital cost of the quarters
options.D: They require no examination of their financial implications at all

e: Residential quarters works, though excepted from the normal remunerativeness test, must satisfy that the assessed rent recoverable yields the prescribed return on the capital cost of the quarters.

q: The rules and instructions relating to the inspection and maintenance of railway bridges are contained in the:

options.A: Indian Railways Works Manual
options.B: Indian Railway Stores Code
options.C: Indian Railways Permanent Way Manual
options.D: Indian Railways Bridge Manual

e: Rules and instructions for inspection and maintenance of railway bridges are contained in the Indian Railways Bridge Manual, distinct from the Works Manual, Stores Code and Permanent Way Manual.

q: Structures provided where a railway line crosses a natural drainage or stream, such as bridges and culverts, are collectively termed:

options.A: Cross-drainage works
options.B: River training works
options.C: Guide works
options.D: Approach works

e: Structures where a railway line crosses natural drainage or a stream, such as bridges and culverts, are collectively termed cross-drainage works.

q: In connection with track renewal works, the abbreviation TBR stands for:

options.A: Track Bed Renewal
options.B: Through Ballast Renewal
options.C: Temporary Ballast Renewal
options.D: Through Blanket Renewal

e: In track renewal, TBR stands for Through Ballast Renewal, that is complete renewal of the ballast cushion through the length, distinct from through sleeper or rail renewal.

q: A 'kink' in the alignment of a railway track is:

options.A: The gradual curvature provided over the length of a curve
options.B: The depression of the rail ends at a rail joint
options.C: An abrupt angular deviation in the alignment of the track, usually occurring at a rail joint
options.D: The widening of the gauge provided on a curve

e: A kink is an abrupt angular deviation in the alignment of the track, usually occurring at a rail joint, as per the Permanent Way Manual track geometry terms.

q: 'Twist' in the geometry of a railway track refers to:

options.A: The rate of change of cross-level along the track, that is, the difference in cross-levels at two points a short distance apart
options.B: The rotation of a rail about its own longitudinal axis
options.C: The difference between the cant at the two ends of a curve
options.D: The lateral shifting of the track as a whole on its formation

e: Twist is the rate of change of cross-level along the track, measured as the difference in cross-levels at two points a short distance apart, as per the Permanent Way Manual.

q: 'Turfing' provided on the slopes of an embankment or a cutting consists of:

options.A: Stone pitching laid on the slope to protect it from erosion
options.B: Concrete slabs laid over the slope of the embankment
options.C: Grass sods laid on the slope to protect it against erosion by rain
options.D: A boulder apron provided at the toe of the slope

e: Turfing consists of grass sods laid on the slopes of an embankment or cutting to protect the slope against erosion by rain.

q: A 'cold joint' in concrete work is a joint which is formed when:

options.A: Concrete is placed during very cold weather
options.B: Fresh concrete is placed against concrete which has already set, so that the two do not bond monolithically unless the joint is specially treated
options.C: An expansion joint is filled with a joint filler material
options.D: Two precast concrete units are joined together at the site

e: A cold joint forms when fresh concrete is placed against concrete that has already set, so the two do not bond monolithically unless the joint is specially treated.

q: The California Bearing Ratio (CBR) test is used in connection with railway formation and pavement design in order to evaluate the:

options.A: Density of the ballast cushion under the sleepers
options.B: Strength of the rails used in the track
options.C: Bearing strength of the subgrade soil
options.D: Hardness of the aggregates used in concrete

e: The California Bearing Ratio (CBR) test evaluates the bearing strength of the subgrade soil and is used in railway formation and pavement design.

q: The grade of concrete, such as M-20, denotes the:

options.A: Quantity of cement contained in one cubic metre of the concrete
options.B: Water-cement ratio adopted for the mix
options.C: Nominal size of the coarse aggregate used in the mix
options.D: Characteristic compressive strength, in newtons per square millimetre, attained by the concrete at 28 days

e: The grade of concrete such as M-20 denotes its characteristic compressive strength in newtons per square millimetre attained at 28 days, here 20 N per sq mm.

q: Distribution reinforcement provided in a reinforced cement concrete slab, in addition to the main reinforcement, serves mainly to:

options.A: Distribute concentrated loads over the slab and to resist shrinkage and temperature stresses
options.B: Resist the shear forces at the supports of the slab
options.C: Replace the main reinforcement at the mid-span of the slab
options.D: Increase the effective depth of the slab section

e: Distribution reinforcement in an RCC slab distributes concentrated loads over the slab and resists shrinkage and temperature stresses, in addition to the main reinforcement.

q: The formwork (centering and shuttering) supporting freshly placed concrete is struck, that is removed, only after:

options.A: The concrete has been placed and finished on the surface
options.B: The concrete has attained sufficient strength to support itself and the loads coming on it, and the permission of the Engineer is obtained
options.C: The final bill of the work has been prepared
options.D: The contractor finds it convenient to shift the formwork to another work

e: Formwork supporting freshly placed concrete is struck only after the concrete has attained sufficient strength to support itself and the loads on it, and with the permission of the Engineer.

q: Expansion joints are provided in concrete structures and buildings primarily in order to:

options.A: Facilitate the placing of concrete in successive lifts
options.B: Provide a passage for cables and pipes through the structure
options.C: Mark the place where the agency executing the work is changed
options.D: Allow the free expansion and contraction of the structure due to changes of temperature and thereby prevent cracking

e: Expansion joints allow free expansion and contraction of the structure due to temperature changes and thereby prevent cracking of concrete structures and buildings.

q: Compaction of earthwork in an embankment yields the maximum dry density when the soil is compacted at its:

options.A: Liquid limit
options.B: Optimum moisture content
options.C: Saturation moisture content
options.D: Natural moisture content in all cases, whatever it may be

e: Compaction yields maximum dry density when the soil is compacted at its optimum moisture content, as established by the compaction (Proctor) test.

q: The filling of a railway embankment through a contractor is required to be carried out:

options.A: In successive layers of limited thickness, each layer being compacted to the specified density before the next layer is laid over it
options.B: By dumping the earth to the full height at one place and rolling only the top surface
options.C: Without compaction of the intermediate layers, compaction being needed only of the top layer
options.D: By watering the finished top surface of the embankment alone

e: Embankment filling must be done in successive layers of limited thickness, each layer compacted to the specified density before the next layer is laid, as per the Works Manual earthwork provisions.

q: A 'breast wall' provided in railway earthwork is a wall which is built:

options.A: At the toe of an embankment to retain the earth filling of the embankment
options.B: On the hill side, to retain and protect the slope of the cutting or of the ground above the formation
options.C: Across a stream at the site of a bridge to divert its flow
options.D: Along the edge of a station platform to retain the platform filling

e: A breast wall is built on the hill side to retain and protect the slope of the cutting or of the ground above the formation; a wall at the toe retaining embankment filling is a toe or retaining wall.

q: The downstream end of a bridge pier, which is shaped so as to minimise the eddies formed as the water leaves the pier, is known as the:

options.A: Cut water of the pier
options.B: Starling of the pier
options.C: Ease water of the pier
options.D: Fender of the pier

e: The downstream end of a bridge pier, shaped to minimise eddies as water leaves the pier, is the ease water; the upstream end that cuts the flow is the cut water.

q: Stretcher bars provided in a turnout (points and crossings) serve to:

options.A: Fasten the rails of the turnout to the sleepers below them
options.B: Connect the stock rail with the check rail of the turnout
options.C: Lock the points electrically with the signals of the station
options.D: Connect the two tongue rails of the switch so that they maintain the correct distance apart and move together

e: Stretcher bars connect the two tongue rails of a switch so that they maintain the correct distance apart and move together, as per the Permanent Way Manual.

q: Wing rails provided at a crossing (frog) in a turnout serve to:

options.A: Guide the flange of the wheel and support the wheel as it passes over the gap at the nose of the crossing
options.B: Fasten the crossing to the sleepers on which it rests
options.C: Connect the two tongue rails of the switch together
options.D: Prevent the creep of the running rails through the turnout

e: Wing rails at a crossing guide the flange of the wheel and support the wheel as it passes over the gap at the nose of the crossing (frog).

q: 'Negative cant' (negative superelevation) arises in connection with a turnout when:

options.A: No cant at all is provided on a length of straight track
options.B: A diverging line curves away in the opposite sense from a main line which is laid with cant, so that the outer rail of the diverging line is effectively the lower rail
options.C: The cant provided on a curve is more than what is required for the slower trains on it
options.D: The gauge of the track is widened on a sharp curve

e: Negative cant arises when a diverging line curves away in the opposite sense from a canted main line, so the outer rail of the diverging line is effectively the lower rail.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. In a deck-type girder bridge, the track is carried on the top of the girders.
2. In a through-type girder bridge, the train passes between the girders, the track being carried at about their bottom level.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Both are correct: in a deck-type girder bridge the track is carried on top of the girders, and in a through-type bridge the train passes between the girders with the track at about their bottom level.

q: A 'piece-work' arrangement adopted for petty works means that:

options.A: The contractor is paid a single lump sum for all the petty works of the year
options.B: The work is executed by departmental labour engaged on piece rates
options.C: The contractor is engaged only for providing labour for the work
options.D: Specified items of work are executed at the agreed rates for the quantities actually done, the work being ordered as and when required, without a separate formal contract for a definite total quantity

e: Piece-work means specified items are executed at agreed rates for quantities actually done, the work being ordered as and when required, without a separate formal contract for a definite total quantity, a method used for petty works.

q: Where an authority is not competent under the Schedule of Powers to sanction a proposal:

options.A: The concurrence of Finance to the proposal does not cure the defect, and the sanction of the authority competent for the proposal is still required
options.B: The concurrence of Finance by itself makes the sanction of that authority valid
options.C: The recommendation of the Tender Committee makes the sanction valid
options.D: The sanction becomes valid if sufficient funds are available in the grant

e: Finance concurrence does not cure lack of competence: where an authority is not competent under the Schedule of Powers, the sanction of the authority competent for the proposal is still required.

q: Tools and plant held in the charge of a sectional official of a Railway are subject to:

options.A: No verification after they are first taken on charge by him
options.B: Periodical, ordinarily annual, verification, shortages or damage noticed being brought to account and dealt with under the rules
options.C: Verification only by the contractor to whom they are issued for a work
options.D: Verification only at the time when they are proposed to be condemned

e: Tools and plant in the charge of a sectional official are subject to periodical, ordinarily annual, verification, and shortages or damage noticed are brought to account and dealt with under the rules, as per the Engineering Code.

q: Articles of a durable nature which are not consumed in use, such as tools, instruments and furniture held in an office or a section, are accounted for in the:

options.A: Material-at-Site account of the works under execution
options.B: Works Register maintained for works expenditure
options.C: Dead Stock Register maintained for such articles
options.D: Contractor's Ledger maintained in the accounts office

e: Durable articles not consumed in use, such as tools, instruments and furniture, are dead stock. Under the Engineering Code they are accounted for in the Dead Stock Register of the office or section holding them, not in the Material-at-Site account or Works Register, which cover materials and works expenditure.

q: In the analysis of rates for an item of work, the labour cost of the item is worked out with reference to:

options.A: The number of labourers whom the contractor proposes to engage on the work
options.B: The wages actually paid by the contractor on a similar work executed earlier
options.C: The attendance of labour recorded in the muster rolls of the work
options.D: The standard out-turn of labour, that is, the quantity of work of that item expected from a unit or gang of labour in a day

e: In rate analysis, labour cost is built up from the standard out-turn, that is the quantity of an item a unit or gang of labour is expected to turn out in a day, combined with the wage rates. The contractor's actual deployment or past payments do not fix the analysed rate.

q: Gradient posts or boards provided along a railway track indicate:

options.A: The distance from that point to the next station on the line
options.B: The speed restriction in force over the section ahead
options.C: The boundary of the railway land adjoining the track
options.D: The gradient, that is the rise or fall, of the track at and beyond that point, for the guidance of the train crew

e: Gradient posts or boards erected along the track show the gradient, the rise or fall of the track, at and beyond that point. They guide the train crew in handling the train over rising or falling stretches; they do not show distances, speed restrictions or land boundaries.

q: 'Coping' provided on the top of a parapet or an exposed wall of a building serves to:

options.A: Carry the load of the roof resting on the wall
options.B: Protect the top of the wall and throw off the rainwater falling on it, preventing its ingress into the wall
options.C: Support the lintels provided over the openings in the wall
options.D: Bond together the two faces of a cavity wall

e: Coping is the protective course laid on top of a parapet or exposed wall. Its function is to protect the wall top and throw off rainwater, preventing water from entering and damaging the wall below.

q: Materials purchased directly for a specific work, without passing through the stock of a stores depot, are charged to the work:

options.A: At the book average rate of the stores depot, plus the percentage charges on stores
options.B: At the market rate prevailing on the date on which they are consumed
options.C: At their actual cost, including freight and carriage, the percentage (overhead) charges on stores being leviable on issues made from stores stock
options.D: At the fixed issue rates given in the schedule of departmental materials in all cases

e: Materials bought directly for a specific work, without passing through stores stock, are charged to the work at their actual cost including freight and carriage. The percentage overhead charges on stores apply only to issues made from stores stock, not to such direct purchases.

q: In the terminology of the General Financial Rules, the security taken from a contractor for the due performance of a contract is referred to as:

options.A: Bid security
options.B: Retention money
options.C: Earnest money
options.D: Performance security

e: Under the General Financial Rules, the security furnished by a contractor to guarantee due performance of the contract is called performance security. It is distinct from bid security or earnest money, which secures the bid itself, and from retention money withheld from bills.

q: Ballast or boulders supplied by a contractor and stacked at the site of a work are measured by stack measurement, and the quantity for which payment is made is arrived at:

options.A: After making the prescribed deduction for voids from the gross measured volume of the stacks
options.B: By counting the number of stacks in which the material is supplied
options.C: At the full gross volume of the stacks, without any deduction
options.D: From the carrying capacity of the wagons in which the material was brought

e: Ballast and boulders supplied in stacks are paid for on stack measurement after making the prescribed deduction for voids from the gross measured volume of the stacks, since loose stacking contains empty spaces. Payment is not made on the full gross volume.

q: High Strength Friction Grip (HSFG) bolts used in the connections of steel structures transfer the load between the connected members primarily through:

options.A: Friction between the connected plates, developed by the high clamping force with which the bolts are tightened
options.B: Bearing of the shank of the bolt against the sides of the bolt holes
options.C: Welding of the heads of the bolts to the connected plates
options.D: Adhesion of the paint applied at the joint after erection

e: HSFG bolts are tightened to a high clamping force, and the load between the connected plates is transferred by the friction developed between them. The bolt shank does not bear against the hole sides in the initial load transfer, which is what makes the joint slip-resistant.

q: A plasticiser admixture added to a concrete mix serves to:

options.A: Accelerate the setting of the concrete in all cases
options.B: Increase the quantity of water required to make the mix workable
options.C: Increase the workability of the mix without increasing its water content, so that the strength of the concrete is not reduced
options.D: Impart a colour to the finished surface of the concrete

e: A plasticiser increases the workability of a concrete mix without adding extra water. Because the water-cement ratio is not raised, the strength of the concrete is not reduced, unlike simply adding more water to make the mix workable.

q: On completion of the final location survey of a proposed new railway line, the land plans and schedules prepared from that survey serve as the basis for:

options.A: Inviting tenders for the construction of the line
options.B: Fixing the rates in the schedule of rates for the work
options.C: Sanctioning the completion report of the line
options.D: The proceedings for the acquisition of the land required for the line

e: The land plans and schedules prepared from the final location survey show the land required for the proposed line plot by plot. They form the basis for the land acquisition proceedings under the applicable land acquisition law.

q: When the site of a work is handed over to the contractor for starting the work:

options.A: The handing over is recorded in writing, signed on behalf of the Railways and by the contractor, so that the date from which the site was available to him is on record
options.B: No record of the handing over is kept, the possession of the site being a purely oral matter
options.C: The contractor is deemed to have taken possession of the site on the date of opening of the tenders
options.D: The site is deemed to have been handed over on the date of sanction of the estimate

e: Handing over of the site to the contractor is recorded in writing, signed on behalf of the Railways and by the contractor. This record fixes the date from which the site was available to him, which is relevant to the completion period and any claim of hindrance.

q: Pre-construction anti-termite treatment provided in a new building work consists of:

options.A: Spraying the finished walls of the building after it is occupied
options.B: Chemical treatment of the soil under and around the foundations and floors, carried out before the construction over them, so as to create a barrier against termites
options.C: Painting the wooden joinery of the building with coal tar after its completion
options.D: Providing a damp proof course in the walls at the plinth level

e: Pre-construction anti-termite treatment is the chemical treatment of the soil under and around the foundations and floors, done before construction over them. It creates a chemical barrier that prevents termites from reaching the building from the ground.

q: Annual (ordinary) repair estimates for railway buildings are ordinarily framed on the basis of:

options.A: Detailed measurement of every item of repair in every year
options.B: The original cost of construction of the building concerned
options.C: Yardsticks, that is unit rates such as a rate per unit of plinth area, prescribed for different types of buildings
options.D: The rates quoted by the contractor holding the zonal contract

e: Annual ordinary repair estimates for buildings are framed on yardsticks, that is unit rates such as a rate per unit of plinth area prescribed for different types of buildings. Detailed measurement of every repair item each year is not practicable, so the yardstick basis is used.

q: In the estimate of the cost of a major project having a long period of construction, a provision for price escalation during the construction period is made in the project estimate itself in order to:

options.A: Pay price variation to the contractor a second time, in addition to the contract clause
options.B: Replace the price variation clause to be included in the contracts for the project
options.C: Arrive at a realistic total cost of the project at the prices expected to prevail during the period of its execution
options.D: Meet the departmental charges leviable on the works of the project

e: A provision for price escalation in a long-duration project estimate is made so that the sanctioned cost reflects the prices expected to prevail during execution, giving a realistic total project cost. It is separate from, and not a substitute for, the price variation clause in individual contracts.

q: A 'toe drain' provided at the foot (toe) of a railway embankment serves to:

options.A: Carry the track cables laid across the formation
options.B: Collect the surface and seepage water coming from the embankment and lead it away, so that the toe of the embankment is kept drained
options.C: Mark the boundary of the railway land at the foot of the embankment
options.D: Drain the water collected in the ballast cushion directly

e: A toe drain at the foot of an embankment collects surface and seepage water coming from the embankment and leads it away. Keeping the toe drained protects the embankment base from softening and erosion.

q: In the survey and levelling of a proposed railway work, a 'bench mark' is:

options.A: A mark made on the rail head to indicate the centre line of the track
options.B: A fixed point of known elevation (reduced level), used as the reference for determining the levels of other points
options.C: A board fixed at a station showing the gradient of the line
options.D: The deepest point up to which the foundation of a structure is to be taken

e: A bench mark is a fixed point of known elevation, or reduced level, established during survey and levelling. All other levels in the work are determined with reference to it.

q: The distance of a point on a proposed railway line, measured along the alignment from the starting point of the survey, is known as its:

options.A: Chainage
options.B: Reduced level
options.C: Formation width
options.D: Bearing

e: The distance of a point measured along the alignment from the starting point of the survey is its chainage. It locates the point along the line, whereas reduced level gives its height and bearing its direction.

q: Consider the following statements: 1. A contour line on a survey plan joins points which are at the same elevation. 2. Where the contour lines on a plan are spaced closely together, the ground is steeper than where they are spaced widely apart. Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Both statements are correct. A contour line joins points of equal elevation, and the spacing of contours shows the slope: closely spaced contours mean steep ground and widely spaced contours mean flat ground.

q: Consider the following statements: 1. A longitudinal section of a proposed railway line shows the profile of the ground and the proposed formation levels along the alignment of the line. 2. A cross-section shows the profile of the ground and the formation at right angles to the alignment, at a particular chainage. Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Both statements are correct. A longitudinal section shows ground and formation profile along the alignment, while a cross-section shows the profile at right angles to the alignment at a particular chainage. Together they define the earthwork of the line.

q: 'Buckling' of a length of long welded track in hot weather refers to:

options.A: The wearing away of the rail head by the passage of trains
options.B: The gradual longitudinal movement of the rails through the sleepers
options.C: The formation of cracks across the head of the rail
options.D: The lateral displacement of the track out of its alignment, caused by the compressive forces set up in the rails when their thermal expansion is restrained

e: Buckling is the lateral displacement of long welded track out of alignment in hot weather. When thermal expansion of the rails is restrained, large compressive forces build up and the track can suddenly shift sideways.

q: 'Adzing' of wooden sleepers, carried out before the rails are laid on them, consists of:

options.A: Treating the sleepers with a preservative to protect them against termites and decay
options.B: Cutting a slope at the seat of the rail on the sleeper, so that the rail is given the prescribed inward inclination when laid
options.C: Boring holes in the sleepers for the dog spikes which fasten the rails
options.D: Trimming the ends of the sleepers square so that they line up uniformly

e: Adzing of wooden sleepers is cutting a slope at the rail seat so that the rail, when laid, gets the prescribed inward inclination, normally 1 in 20. It is not preservative treatment or boring for spikes.

q: A 'pusher gradient' on a railway section is a gradient which is:

options.A: So steep that trains can negotiate it only with the assistance of an additional (pusher or banker) engine
options.B: The flattest gradient provided anywhere on the section
options.C: The gradient provided inside a station yard for shunting purposes
options.D: A falling gradient on which trains are controlled wholly by their brakes

e: A pusher gradient is so steep that a train cannot negotiate it with its own locomotive alone and needs an additional pusher or banker engine. It is steeper than the ruling gradient workable by a single engine.

q: A 'vertical curve' is provided on a railway line at a point where:

options.A: The line changes from broad gauge to metre gauge
options.B: A level crossing is to be widened for road traffic
options.C: Two tracks cross each other at different levels
options.D: Two gradients of different inclinations meet, in order to ease the change from one gradient to the other

e: A vertical curve is provided where two gradients of different inclination meet. It eases the change from one gradient to the other so that trains pass smoothly without sudden change of slope.

q: The 'sighting distance' required to be available at a level crossing is:

options.A: The length of the longest train which passes over the crossing
options.B: The unobstructed distance over which the driver of a train and the user of the road can see each other (or the train) in time to cross or stop safely
options.C: The distance between the gate lodge and the nearest signal
options.D: The width of the road where it crosses the railway track

e: Sighting distance at a level crossing is the unobstructed distance over which the train driver and the road user can see each other, or the train, in time to cross or stop safely. Adequate sighting distance is a basic safety requirement at crossings.

q: 'Through packing' in the maintenance of a railway track means:

options.A: Packing of the ballast under every sleeper throughout a length of track, carried out systematically to restore its level and alignment
options.B: Packing of the ballast under a few isolated sleepers only, where a defect is noticed
options.C: Filling of ballast between the two rails up to the top of the rail head
options.D: Compaction of the earthwork of the formation before the ballast is spread

e: Through packing is the systematic packing of ballast under every sleeper throughout a length of track to restore its level and alignment. Packing only isolated defective sleepers is spot attention, not through packing.

q: The ballast provided beyond the ends of the sleepers, forming the shoulder of the ballast section, serves mainly to:

options.A: Provide a footpath for the staff patrolling the section
options.B: Store the surplus ballast required for future renewals
options.C: Resist the lateral movement of the track and thereby help the track to retain its alignment
options.D: Drain the rain water away from the centre of the track

e: The ballast shoulder beyond the sleeper ends resists lateral movement of the track. This lateral resistance helps the track, especially long welded track, retain its alignment against thermal and dynamic forces.

q: 'Boxing' of the ballast in a length of track consists of:

options.A: Transporting the ballast to the site in boxes carried on wagons
options.B: Screening the ballast to remove the accumulated dirt and muck from it
options.C: Testing the depth of the ballast cushion at intervals with a gauge
options.D: Filling the ballast into the spaces between the sleepers (cribs) and at the shoulders, and dressing it to the prescribed profile

e: Boxing of ballast means filling ballast into the cribs between sleepers and at the shoulders and dressing it to the prescribed ballast profile. It completes the ballast section after packing.

q: An elastomeric bearing provided under the girder of a bridge is a bearing made of:

options.A: Alternate layers of rubber and steel plates, which allows the movement and rotation of the girder by deformation of the rubber
options.B: A curved steel plate resting on cylindrical rollers of hardened steel
options.C: A block of plain concrete cast along with the bed block of the pier
options.D: Timber packing pieces driven tight between the girder and the pier cap

e: An elastomeric bearing consists of alternate layers of rubber and steel plates bonded together. The girder's movements and rotations are accommodated by deformation of the rubber layers, while the steel plates give it vertical stiffness.

q: A 'return wall' provided at the abutment of a bridge is a wall which:

options.A: Is built across the stream below the bridge to raise the water level
options.B: Extends back from the abutment into the approach embankment, roughly parallel to the track, and retains the filling of the approach
options.C: Connects the tops of two adjacent piers above the water level
options.D: Is built in front of the abutment to protect it from the direct impact of flood water

e: A return wall extends back from the bridge abutment into the approach embankment, roughly parallel to the track. It retains the filling of the approach behind the abutment.

q: An 'approach slab' provided at the end of a bridge, behind the abutment, serves to:

options.A: Anchor the girders of the bridge against uplift during a flood
options.B: Carry the expansion joint between the bridge and the approach road
options.C: Support the track over the zone of back-filling behind the abutment, so that settlement of the filling does not produce a sudden dip in the track at the bridge end
options.D: Provide a platform from which the bearings of the bridge are inspected

e: An approach slab supports the track over the backfill zone behind an abutment. It bridges over the filling so that settlement of that filling does not cause a sudden dip in the track at the bridge end.

q: 'Trolley refuges' provided on long bridges are:

options.A: Sheds at the end of the bridge for storing the trolleys used by inspection staff
options.B: Recesses in the parapet where the rails of the bridge are stored as spare
options.C: Chambers below the deck of the bridge in which drainage water is collected
options.D: Recesses or platforms provided at intervals along the bridge, into which staff working on or inspecting the bridge can step to stand clear of a passing train

e: Trolley refuges are recesses or platforms provided at intervals on long bridges. Staff working on or inspecting the bridge can step into them to stand clear of a passing train.

q: In the design of a bridge across a stream, the 'freeboard' is the clearance provided between:

options.A: The highest flood level at the bridge and the underside (soffit) of the girders
options.B: The bed of the stream and the bottom of the foundations of the piers
options.C: The top of the rail on the bridge and the top of the parapet
options.D: The two tracks carried on a double-line bridge

e: Freeboard of a bridge is the clearance between the highest flood level and the underside, or soffit, of the girders. It ensures flood water and floating debris pass without striking the superstructure.

q: A 'drop wall' provided at the end of the floor (apron) of a culvert or a small bridge is a wall which:

options.A: Is built above the floor to divide the flow of water between the vents
options.B: Is taken down below the level of the floor at its edges, so that scour of the bed cannot undermine the floor
options.C: Supports the wing walls of the culvert against overturning
options.D: Marks the boundary up to which the bed of the stream may be deepened

e: A drop wall is taken down below floor level at the end of the floor or apron of a culvert or small bridge. It prevents scour of the bed from undermining and washing out the floor.

q: The 'plinth protection' provided around a building consists of:

options.A: A coat of water-proofing compound applied to the outer face of the plinth
options.B: A course of dense concrete laid inside the plinth below the floor of the building
options.C: A paved apron laid on the ground all along the outside of the building, to prevent rain water from seeping into the soil next to the foundations
options.D: An extra thickness of the walls provided at the plinth level of the building

e: Plinth protection is a paved apron laid on the ground all along the outside of a building. It prevents rainwater from seeping into the soil next to the foundations and weakening or settling them.

q: A sunshade (chajja) provided over a door or a window of a building is:

options.A: A sloping roof built over the whole verandah of the building
options.B: A curtain wall of glass provided on the sunny face of the building
options.C: A grille of iron bars fixed in the opening for the security of the room
options.D: A projection of the slab or masonry over the opening, which protects the opening from the sun and from rain water

e: A sunshade or chajja is a projection of slab or masonry over a door or window opening. It protects the opening from direct sun and from rainwater running down the wall face.

q: A 'cornice' provided in a building is:

options.A: A projecting course or moulding at the top of a wall, where the wall meets the roof, which also throws rain water clear of the face of the wall
options.B: A recess formed in a wall for keeping a cupboard or a shelf
options.C: The horizontal member placed across the top of a door frame
options.D: A beam provided below a slab to support a partition wall above it

e: A cornice is a projecting course or moulding at the top of a wall where it meets the roof. Besides its architectural finish, it throws rainwater clear of the face of the wall.

q: 'Skirting' provided in a room of a building is:

options.A: The finish given to the ceiling of the room along its edges
options.B: The finish provided at the bottom of the walls of the room, for a small height above the floor, to protect the base of the wall and cover its junction with the floor
options.C: A board fixed on the wall for displaying notices and circulars
options.D: The slope given to the floor of the room for draining out the wash water

e: Skirting is the finish provided at the bottom of the internal walls, for a small height above the floor. It protects the base of the wall from damage and moisture during cleaning and covers the junction of wall and floor.

q: 'Random rubble masonry' used in the construction of walls and foundations consists of:

options.A: Stones dressed to a uniform size and laid in regular courses throughout
options.B: Bricks laid on edge in a pattern of alternating headers and stretchers
options.C: Rough, undressed stones laid in mortar in irregular courses, without uniformity of size or shape
options.D: Large concrete blocks cast at the site and laid without mortar in the joints

e: Random rubble masonry is built of rough, undressed stones of irregular size and shape laid in mortar in irregular courses. It is distinct from coursed or ashlar masonry where stones are dressed and laid uniformly.

q: In brickwork, 'English bond' is a bond in which:

options.A: Every course consists of stretchers only, the bricks being laid lengthwise
options.B: Every course consists of headers only, the bricks being laid across the wall
options.C: Stretchers and headers are laid alternately in the same course throughout
options.D: Courses of headers and courses of stretchers are laid alternately, one above the other

e: In English bond, courses of headers and courses of stretchers are laid alternately one above the other. Alternating headers and stretchers within the same course is Flemish bond, not English bond.

q: A retarding admixture (retarder) added to a concrete mix serves to:

options.A: Slow down the setting of the cement, which is useful in hot weather and where the concrete has to be transported over a long distance
options.B: Increase the early strength of the concrete so that the formwork can be struck sooner
options.C: Make the concrete water-tight by filling the pores of the mix
options.D: Give a colour to the concrete used in the exposed faces of a structure

e: A retarding admixture slows down the setting of cement. It is used in hot weather and where concrete must be transported over a long distance, so that the mix remains workable until placed.

q: The 'lap length' provided where two reinforcement bars in a structure are joined to one another is:

options.A: The length of the bar which is bent up at the ends of a beam
options.B: The length over which the two bars are overlapped, so that the force in one bar is transferred to the other through the surrounding concrete
options.C: The length of the bar embedded in the concrete beyond the face of the support
options.D: The distance between two adjacent bars placed side by side in a slab

e: Lap length is the length over which two reinforcement bars are overlapped where they are joined. The overlap lets the force in one bar transfer to the other through bond with the surrounding concrete.

q: An 'isolated footing' provided in the foundation of a building is:

options.A: A continuous footing running under the whole length of a load-bearing wall
options.B: A raft of concrete spread under the whole area of the building
options.C: A separate footing provided under a single column, which spreads the load of that column over a sufficient area of the soil
options.D: A footing in which two columns standing close together share one common base

e: An isolated footing is a separate footing under a single column. It spreads that column's load over a sufficient area of soil so that the pressure stays within the safe bearing capacity.

q: A reinforced cement concrete slab is described as a 'two-way slab' when it is:

options.A: Cast in two separate layers, one above the other
options.B: Supported on two sides only and spans in one direction between them
options.C: Provided with two separate layers of reinforcement, at its top and its bottom
options.D: Supported on all four sides and spans in both directions, the main reinforcement being provided in both directions

e: A two-way slab is supported on all four sides and spans in both directions, with main reinforcement provided in both directions. A slab supported on two sides only spans one way and is a one-way slab.

q: The 'gradation' of the aggregate used in concrete refers to:

options.A: The distribution of the particles of the aggregate by size, a well-graded aggregate containing particles ranging from coarse to fine so that they pack densely
options.B: The classification of the aggregate according to the quarry from which it is obtained
options.C: The extent to which the surface of the aggregate is smooth or rough
options.D: The proportion in which the aggregate is mixed with the cement in the concrete

e: Gradation of aggregate is the distribution of its particles by size. A well-graded aggregate, with particles ranging from coarse to fine, packs densely with fewer voids, giving stronger and more economical concrete.

q: The 'frog' of a brick is:

options.A: The tool used for cutting the bricks to shape at the site of work
options.B: The depression formed on one face of the brick, which provides a key for the mortar and usually carries the name of the maker
options.C: The mark left on a brick which has been over-burnt in the kiln
options.D: The hollow formed in a wall where a brick has been removed for a fixture

e: The frog of a brick is the depression formed on one of its faces. It provides a key for the mortar joint and usually carries the maker's name or mark.

q: In a staircase, the 'riser' is:

options.A: The horizontal surface of a step on which the foot is placed
options.B: The railing provided along the open side of the staircase
options.C: The vertical face of a step, that is, the height between two successive steps (treads)
options.D: The flat platform provided at the turn of a staircase for resting

e: The riser of a step is its vertical face, that is the height between two successive treads. The horizontal surface on which the foot rests is the tread, not the riser.

q: Consider the following statements: 1. In earthwork, the 'lead' is the horizontal distance over which the excavated earth is transported for use in an embankment or for disposal. 2. In earthwork, the 'lift' is the vertical height through which the excavated earth is raised. Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Both statements are correct. In earthwork, lead is the horizontal distance over which excavated earth is transported, and lift is the vertical height through which it is raised; rates for earthwork are framed with reference to lead and lift.

q: The 'formation width' of a railway line is:

options.A: The distance between the centres of the two tracks on a double line
options.B: The total width of the land acquired for the railway at a place
options.C: The depth of the ballast and the sleepers together, measured below the rail
options.D: The width of the prepared top surface of the embankment (or the bottom of the cutting) on which the ballast and the track are laid

e: Formation width is the width of the prepared top surface of the embankment, or the bottom of the cutting, on which the ballast and track are laid. It is narrower than the total land width acquired for the railway.

q: 'Rain cuts' which appear on the slopes of a railway embankment or cutting are:

options.A: Gullies or channels washed out on the slope by rain water flowing down it, which are filled up and restored during maintenance
options.B: Drains dug deliberately across the slope to lead the rain water away
options.C: Cracks which appear across the top of the embankment in dry weather
options.D: Benches cut into a high slope to make it stable against sliding

e: Rain cuts are gullies or channels washed out on the slopes of an embankment or cutting by rainwater flowing down the slope. They are filled up and the slope restored during maintenance; they are not deliberately dug drains.

q: Where a drawing of a work shows a dimension both by figures written on it and by the scale of the drawing, and the two do not agree, the position under the contract is that:

options.A: The dimension obtained by scaling the drawing is followed
options.B: The figured dimension written on the drawing is followed, in preference to the scaled dimension
options.C: The contractor may follow whichever of the two suits him
options.D: The average of the two dimensions is adopted for execution

e: Where a figured dimension on a drawing differs from the dimension obtained by scaling, the figured dimension governs. This is the standard rule in works contracts, since scaling a drawing is liable to error from printing and paper distortion.
